propositions: A completion close that reads HEAD independently during verify and sign phases can be split by an unrelated concurrent commit, causing the ticket to close without a completion signature despite verification succeeding on a different tree state.

When a TOCTOU drift occurs between verify and sign, rebar closes the ticket anyway with an invalid attestation and suggests re-closing as recovery, which is a no-op because the ticket is already closed.
The default (no --ref) code path pins no revision across verify+sign+close, allowing HEAD to move between phases; only the explicit --ref code path atomically pins the revision.
Recovery options for an already-closed-but-unsigned completion are limited to --force-close or manual manifest fabrication, with no idiomatic non-force recovery analogous to resign_plan_review.
A benign race with an unrelated in-flight commit should not invalidate a completion attestation that was verified against its real merged work.
